newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Scitex to unveil new products.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Scitex to unveil new products.

text.p: Scitex Corp will unveil a series of new products at this week's Imprinta printing and publishing trade fair in Germany which it hopes will firmly place its core graphic arts business on the road to recovery.

At a news conference on Sunday the Israeli maker of pre-press, digital printing and digital video systems demonstrated one of its new products, the EverSmart line of scanners, that analysts say should boost second half revenues.
In the wake of sharp losses of $4.16 a share last year, Scitex undertook a massive restructuring of its graphic arts business, which accounts for over two thirds of revenues.
It sacked 400 employees and took other measures to cut operating expenses by $10 million per quarter.
The result was a smaller-than-expected loss of $0.17 a share in the first quarter. Equity analysts predict the company will return to profitability by the third quarter.
"Until now we have focused on a reduction in costs. But new products is the other part of our recovery programme," Scitex president and chief executive Yoav Chelouche said.
Michael Nagler, vice president and general manager of graphic arts products, told Reuters that Scitex is investing $80 million a year worldwide in developing new products.
It invested $3 million to $4 million in the EverSmart scanner which uses a new technology called "X-Y technology".

This enables the user to scan optics by moving along both the X and Y axes, providing high resolution scanning regardless of the placement and thickness of the original. This could be used, for example, in making high-quality posters from any size original.

The scanners sell for $30,000 to $40,000. Lior Ma'ayan, marketing director of the output imaging systems division, said there are already 10 clients for the scanner in Israel, which serves as a quasi-beta site for the company's products.
Ma'ayan estimated the Israeli market for its pre-press products totals $7 million to $8 million a year. "In the past year we have taken about 85 percent of that," he said.
The company is also making inroads in the region. Though it has been selling to Egypt since 1994 it now does business in Jordan and recently began direct sales to some Gulf countries, Ma'ayan said.

Another product Scitex will show at Imprinta is the Lotem 800V thermal platesetter, which simplifies pre-press procedures by combining various stages into one. It is expected to hit the market in the first quarter of 1998.

In the third quarter of 1997 Scitex will begin selling a dry-imaging device called the Dolev 2dry filmsetter, which eliminates the need for an external processor. It is the product of an alliance with Imation Corp, a spin-off of Minnesota Mining & Manufacturing Co.
